name: checkov-prismaless
description: Find and fix misconfigurations in infrastructure-as-code manifests like Terraform, Kubernetes, Cloudformation, Serverless framework, Arm templates using Checkov - static analysis for infrastructure as code.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Checkov runs against workspace files and reads its configuration from the workspace, so scanning is only available in trusted workspaces.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Checkov needs the files to be available on disk.

checkov-prismaless.checkovVersion.title: Checkov Version
checkov-prismaless.checkovVersion.markdownDescription: The Checkov version to use, for example `3.2.0`. Leave blank or enter `latest` to use the newest release. Versions older than 2.0.0 are not supported. Checkov is reinstalled when this changes. Run **Checkov: About Checkov** to see the version in use.

checkov-prismaless.disableErrorMessage.title: Disable Error Messages
checkov-prismaless.disableErrorMessage.markdownDescription: Stop showing a pop-up when Checkov fails to install or scan. Errors are still written to the log (**Checkov: Open Log**).

checkov-prismaless.clearCacheUponConfigU.title: Clear Cache on Settings Change
checkov-prismaless.clearCacheUponConfigU.markdownDescription: Clear all cached scan results when a setting or Checkov config file that affects results changes. Results from before the change are never reused either way, so this only frees the space they take.

checkov-prismaless.maximumConcurrentScan.title: Maximum Concurrent Scans
checkov-prismaless.maximumConcurrentScan.markdownDescription: The most files scanned at the same time. When a new scan would go over this limit, the oldest running scan is cancelled. Higher values use more CPU and memory.

checkov-prismaless.scanTimeout.title: Scan Timeout
checkov-prismaless.scanTimeout.markdownDescription: How long, in seconds, a scan can run before it is cancelled.

checkov-prismaless.useDebugLogs.title: Checkov Debug Logs
checkov-prismaless.useDebugLogs.markdownDescription: Run Checkov with debug logging, written to the log (**Checkov: Open Log**). Useful for troubleshooting, but it makes the log much larger.

checkov-prismaless.externalChecksDir.title: External Checks Directory
checkov-prismaless.externalChecksDir.markdownDescription: A directory of custom checks for Checkov to run alongside its built-in ones (`--external-checks-dir`). Checkov runs the Python in this directory. Workspace settings can only point inside the workspace folder, and relative paths are resolved against it. Any other location has to be set in user settings.

checkov-prismaless.useBridgecrewIDs.title: Use Bridgecrew IDs
checkov-prismaless.useBridgecrewIDs.markdownDescription: Report findings with legacy Bridgecrew IDs (`BC_...`) instead of Checkov IDs (`CKV_...`). The severity mappings use Checkov IDs, so findings fall back to the severity Checkov reports, which is often unknown.

checkov-prismaless.certificate.title: CA Certificate
checkov-prismaless.certificate.markdownDescription: Path to a CA certificate file for Checkov to trust (`--ca-certificate`). Only read from user settings, so a workspace cannot change it.

checkov-prismaless.noCertVerify.title: Skip TLS Certificate Verification
checkov-prismaless.noCertVerify.markdownDescription: Turn off TLS certificate verification for Checkov's network requests (`--no-cert-verify`). Only use this for testing, as invalid or forged certificates cannot be detected. Only read from user settings, so a workspace cannot change it.

checkov-prismaless.skipFrameworks.title: Skip Frameworks
checkov-prismaless.skipFrameworks.markdownDescription: Frameworks to leave out of scans, separated by spaces or commas (for example `secrets dockerfile`). Overrides any `skip-framework` in your [Checkov config file](https://github.com/bridgecrewio/checkov?tab=readme-ov-file#configuration-using-a-config-file). See [Checkov frameworks](https://www.checkov.io/2.Basics/CLI%20Command%20Reference.html) for the names.

checkov-prismaless.frameworks.title: Frameworks
checkov-prismaless.frameworks.markdownDescription: Only scan with these frameworks, separated by spaces or commas (for example `terraform kubernetes`). Overrides any `framework` in your [Checkov config file](https://github.com/bridgecrewio/checkov?tab=readme-ov-file#configuration-using-a-config-file). See [Checkov frameworks](https://www.checkov.io/2.Basics/CLI%20Command%20Reference.html) for the names.

checkov-prismaless.skipChecks.title: Skip Checks
checkov-prismaless.skipChecks.markdownDescription:
Check IDs to skip, separated by spaces or commas. Wildcards work, as in the default `BC_LIC*`, which skips licence compliance checks.  

**Priority:** if a `.checkov.yaml` or `.checkov.yml` that applies to the file contains `skip-check`, it takes complete precedence and this setting is ignored. To rely entirely on your config file, clear this setting.

checkov-prismaless.skipPaths.title: Skip Paths
checkov-prismaless.skipPaths.markdownDescription: Glob patterns, relative to the workspace folder, for files that should not be scanned (for example `**/*.md`). The status bar shows when a file is skipped.

checkov-prismaless.minimumSeverity.title: Minimum Severity
checkov-prismaless.minimumSeverity.markdownDescription: Only show findings at or above this severity. `None` shows every finding. Findings with an unknown severity are always shown, and the status bar says when findings are hidden.

checkov-prismaless.dockerSelinux.title: Docker SELinux Handling
checkov-prismaless.dockerSelinux.markdownDescription: How to give the Checkov container access to your files on hosts that enforce SELinux. Only needed if scans fail with permission errors when using Docker.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Mount files without any SELinux option.

Mount the workspace folder with the `z` option. Docker relabels it on the host so containers can read it. The change is recursive and stays after the scan. Files outside the workspace folder are not relabelled, so scanning them needs `disable` instead.
Run the container with `--security-opt label=disable`. Files on the host are left alone and SELinux separation is turned off for the Checkov container only.

scripts.vscode:prepublish: node -e "require('fs').rmSync('out', { recursive: true, force: true })" && npm run compile
scripts.pretest: npm run compile && npm run lint
